name: Hearth Sheets spike corpus (C3.7 / B.7 / Q16)
about: 27 openly licensed public workbooks used by the Sheets spike (BUILD-PLAN C3.7, PRD B.7 part b, Q16) in place of the org's own files, by the owner's choice. Each was saved by Excel, so formula cells carry Excel's computed values, which act as the oracle. Categories: oracle (function test matrices), feature (one import/export structure each), everyday (the kinds of workbook the org uses), performance (large real models), edge (sheet states, links, macros).

fields.id: Corpus id: O = oracle, F = feature, E = everyday, P = performance, X = edge. Gaps in numbering (F05, E03, E04) are files dropped at the licence check.
fields.file: Path inside the corpus. Byte-identical to the pinned source; see sha256.
fields.source: Repository, commit, path and pinned raw URL. fetch.py re-downloads from raw_url and checks sha256.
fields.licence: SPDX id (LicenseRef-PublicDomain-USGov = US federal work, 17 U.S.C. 105), the evidence, and the licence texts in LICENSES/.
fields.attribution: Credit line the licence or publisher asks for; also in NOTICE.md.
fields.application, app_version, excel_saved, s: From analyse_xlsx.py run over files/. 'cells' counts <c> elements, including styled empty cells. Function counts are per formula text, so a shared formula counts once, not once per cell. The analyser folds newer names into SHEET-08 names (STDEV.S, VAR.S, RANK.EQ, CEILING.MATH, FLOOR.MATH, NETWORKDAYS.INTL, WORKDAY.INTL).
fields.sheet08_functions_exact_names: SHEET-08 functions whose own name appears (no folding).
fields.non_empty_cells, max_row, max_col, excel: From the selector's read-only zip/XML scan of the same bytes (same sha256). features_exact corrects the analyser's double counts (pivot tables, external links) and adds hidden and very hidden sheets, chart sheets, notes, threaded comments, hyperlinks, dynamic-array cells, form controls, rich data and the 1904 flag.
fields.tests: What the file is for in the spike.
fields.notes: Corrections and cautions from the licence and provenance checks.

analyser.name: analyse_xlsx.py
analyser.note: Static: unzips and reads XML only; nothing in a workbook is executed. Numeric fields come from it unless the field list says otherwise.
known_limits: Counts pivot-table and external-link relationship parts as well as the parts themselves, so it reports about double (use features_exact).
'cells' includes styled empty <c> elements; use non_empty_cells for SHEET-33 sizing.
Reads only the master text of shared formulas, so function and lookup counts for P01-P03 are far below the per-cell numbers.
Misses mixed-case VBA user-defined functions (=Subsidy(...) in X03).
Does not count x14 conditional-formatting or validation rules, or cross-sheet references inside them (F03 has 12 x14 blocks; F01 has one).
Does not detect Power Query mashups (P03 customXml/item1.xml), sensitivity-label parts (docMetadata/LabelInfo.xml in E01, E12) or add-in parts (xl/webextensions in O04, E06, X02).
Treats docProps <Application> alone as proof of an Excel save; the selector also checked workbook.xml rupBuild/calcId (excel_build).
Folds NETWORKDAYS.INTL and WORKDAY.INTL into NETWORKDAYS and WORKDAY, which are different functions.

sheet08.same_function_note: Counts a SHEET-08 function only when its own name, or Excel's newer name for the same function (STDEV.S, VAR.S, RANK.EQ), appears. NETWORKDAYS is then missing: only NETWORKDAYS.INTL (O03) appears, and the analyser folds it into NETWORKDAYS.

missing: department or project budget (E04 was dropped)
timesheet with overtime pay (E03 was dropped)
shift roster with formulas (hours, OT pay)
inventory / stock list with reorder levels
anything Singapore-specific: S$ formats, day-first dates, en-SG locale, GST, public holidays

generator_spec.name: hearth-perf-gen (to be written and run in the spike; nothing has been generated yet)
generator_spec.purpose: Deterministic workbooks with known values for SHEET-33/34 and B.7's stress case, which no public file provides.
generator_spec.tooling: Python 3 stdlib plus XlsxWriter (BSD-2-Clause), or rust_xlsxwriter (MIT/Apache-2.0); both write a formula together with its saved value. CLI: --profile, --rows, --seed (default 20261011), --out.
generator_spec.determinism: An in-house SplitMix64 PRNG, never Python's random. Integers and 2-decimal amounts; dates as serials 45292-45657 (2024); no volatile functions; fixed docProps (creator 'hearth-perf-gen', fixed dates). The same arguments always give the same sha256.
generator_spec.outputs: The .xlsx, with each formula saved alongside the value the generator computed, plus manifest.json: seed, profile, non-empty cell count, formulas by function, the expected value of each formula cell (or a per-column digest), and 20 scripted edits with the cells each changes and their new values.
generator_spec.excel_twin: Open each file once in desktop Excel, press Ctrl+Alt+F9 and save it as <name>.excel.xlsx. Fix the generator wherever it disagrees with the twin, then use the twin as the oracle, as with the public files.

REF100K: SHEET-34 reference workbook: 100,000 +/-1% non-empty cells; print the exact count.

Tab Data: header row, then rows 2-8001 with A ShipmentID (int), B Date (serial), C Depot (12 codes such as SG-JUR, SG-TUAS, SG-CHANGI), D SKU (400 codes) and E-J Qty/Weight/Cartons/Pallets/Cost/Freight. K2:K8001 =SUM(E2:J2) and L2:L8001 =IF(K2>=$N$1,"Over","OK"). Row 8002 holds column totals =SUM(E2:E8001) for E-K.
Tab Rates: 400 rows of SKU, UnitCost, Category.
Tab Summary: 300 SKUs, each with =XLOOKUP(A2,Rates!$A$2:$A$401,Rates!$B$2:$B$401,"n/a") and =SUMIFS(Data!$E$2:$E$8001,Data!$D$2:$D$8001,A2). Pad with a values block to reach 100,000 cells.
Edits: 10 in Data!E, 5 in Rates!B, 5 to $N$1. Measure per-edit recalculation p50/p95 against 250 ms desktop and 750 ms phone, and open time against 2 s / 4 s using a 50K variant.
B7: Tab Ref: 5,000 rows (A key K00001..., B value, C composite key).

Tab Data: N rows with A key (95% present, 5% missing), B group (1 of 50), C amount, D =XLOOKUP(A2,Ref!A:A,Ref!B:B,"missing") and E =SUMIFS(C:C,B:B,B2), whole columns as in B.7. N = 1,000 / 3,000 / 5,000 / 10,000.
Variants: bounded ranges; INDEX/MATCH; VLOOKUP(...,FALSE); XLOOKUP binary search (search_mode 2) on sorted keys; COUNTIFS in place of SUMIFS; composite key =XLOOKUP(A2&"|"&B2,Ref!C:C,Ref!B:B).

Edits: one Data!C (dirties every SUMIFS), one Ref!B, one Data!A. Record load, first calculation, per-edit recalculation p50/p95 and memory: WebAssembly in a Web Worker on the slowest supported phone, and the Node binding on one server core.
B.7 baselines: IronCalc about 9 s at 5,000 rows and 3.6 s at 3,000; HyperFormula 34 s to load and 7.8 s per edit at 3,000.
LIMITS: Values only, for SHEET-33's warnings and blocks.

Cells: 200,000 non-empty (80% warning), 250,000 (at the cap) and 250,001 (blocked). Rows: one tab of 100,000 rows and one of 100,001. Columns: 200 (A-GR) and 201 (GS). Cell text: 50,000 characters and 50,001. Tabs: 100 and 101.
P1 set: 800,000, 1,000,000 and 1,000,001 cells. A 5 MB XLSX near 250k cells for the 30 s conversion target.
Real files P02 (83% of cap) and P03 (over the P0 cap) complement these.
PATTERNS: Small oracle files cut down from shapes seen in real workbooks: CSE INDEX/MATCH(1,(a=b)*(c=d),0) and MIN/MAX/SUM(IF()) arrays; INDEX(OFFSET(col,,n),row) and whole-column INDEX/MATCH; LOOKUP(C:C,{...},{...}) relying on implicit intersection, and formulas with a leading '+'; GETPIVOTDATA over a small pivot; INDIRECT(ADDRESS()) volatile chains.
For each, record whether Hearth computes the cell or keeps it as a fixed value under SHEET-31, and compare with the Excel twin.
INJECTION: Security, not performance: the CSV-export and Rule 8 cases listed in gaps, written into normal, hidden and very hidden tabs, notes and threaded comments.
